title: The Most Beautiful Child (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: Akbar boasts of his handsome princes and challenges Birbal to find the most beautiful child in Agra. Birbal brings an astonishing answer. [KN]
full_text:
During an afternoon stroll in the palace gardens, Emperor Akbar held his young grandson, Prince Khurram, admiring his fair skin, bright eyes, and silk clothes. Akbar remarked to Birbal: 'Look at this prince! Truly, he is the most beautiful child in all of Hindustan! Have you ever seen a child more radiant?'

Birbal smiled gently: 'Sire, every mother and father sees supreme beauty in their own child. In truth, beauty is in the eyes of love, not in skin or pearls.'

Akbar challenged him: 'Go into Agra today, Birbal, and bring me the most beautiful child in the city! If he surpasses my grandson, I shall reward you!'

Birbal departed into the city. Hours later, he invited Akbar to accompany him in disguise to a poor potter's settlement near the river.

Behind a humble mud hut, playing in the dirt, sat a little toddler. The child was covered in dust, had a running nose, uncombed hair, and dark, sunburnt skin. The child's mother, a tired woman in a patched cotton sari, rushed out, picked up the filthy toddler, kissed his cheeks with overflowing joy, and murmured: 'My little moon! My prince! The sweetest jewel in the whole world!'

Akbar whispered to Birbal in disgust: 'Birbal! Is this the child you brought me to see? He is dirty, plain, and covered in mud! How can you call him beautiful?'

Just then, the mother overheard Akbar's whisper. She turned with flashing eyes, holding her child tightly to her breast:

'How dare you call my baby plain, you stranger! He has the smile of an angel! His laughter fills my heart with sunshine! To me, he is a thousand times more beautiful than any prince who sits in a golden palace!'

Akbar stood silenced. He looked at the radiant joy on the poor mother's face and the pure love in her eyes.

Birbal stepped forward: 'You see, Your Majesty? To this mother, her child is the most beautiful creature in existence. True beauty cannot be measured with a jeweler's scale; it is measured only by the boundless devotion of love.'

Akbar bowed his head in deep humility, gifted the mother a purse of gold coins, and commended Birbal for teaching him the true meaning of beauty.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
